page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Transpiration
steps.margin_note: Four numbered points. Keep the numbering so the second column can mirror it.
lines: 1. Transpiration is the loss of water from the
LIVING tissues of the aerial parts of a plant.
steps.why: Transpiration is controlled by living stomata, so it is a physiological process and necessarily slower than plain evaporation from an open surface.
common_mistakes: Saying transpiration happens from any surface. It happens from LIVING tissue only.
Calling it a physical process. It is PHYSIOLOGICAL, because the plant controls it.

steps.label: Evaporation
steps.margin_note: Mirror the four numbered points exactly. Same order, opposite content.

lines.text: Living and controlled against free and fast

lines: 1. Evaporation is the loss of water from ANY
2. It is a surface level process.
steps.why: Nothing living regulates evaporation, so it is faster and can happen anywhere water meets air — which is every contrast in one cause.
common_mistakes: Saying evaporation happens only from non-living surfaces. It happens from ANY free surface.
Giving fewer than three contrasts. The comparison needs both columns filled.
steps.memory_tip: No living control means nothing to slow it down.
